grammar.countability: countable as a legal agreement; used without an article in expressions such as under contract
grammar.transitivity: transitive or intransitive as a verb, depending on meaning
patterns: enter into / sign / perform a contract
be under contract to + person / organization

usage.noun: A contract is an agreement creating legally enforceable rights or obligations, subject to the requirements of the applicable law.
usage.document: Contract may refer either to the legal agreement itself or to the document recording its terms.
usage.oral_contract: A contract is not necessarily written or signed; oral and conduct-based contracts may be enforceable, although some contracts must satisfy formal requirements.
usage.agreement_distinction: Agreement is broader than contract because not every agreement is intended or legally able to create enforceable obligations.
usage.contracting_verb: To contract with someone means to enter into a legally binding agreement with that person or organization.
usage.commission_verb: To contract someone to do work means to formally engage that person or business to perform it.
usage.shrink_verb: When a muscle, material, or volume contracts, it becomes shorter, tighter, or smaller.
usage.disease_verb: To contract a disease or infection means to become infected with or develop it.
usage.pronunciation: The noun is stressed on the first syllable, while the verb is normally stressed on the second syllable.

ja: 当事者間に法的に強制可能な権利・義務を生じさせる契約
契約条件を記載した契約書
人・会社などと契約を締結する
人・会社に契約によって業務を依頼する
病気・感染症にかかる
筋肉・器官などが収縮する
物質・体積などが縮小する
借金・義務などを負う
en: an agreement creating rights or obligations enforceable by law
a written document recording the terms of a legal agreement
to enter into a contract with a person or organization
to formally engage a person or company to perform work
to become infected with or develop a disease
for a muscle or organ, to become shorter or tighter
for a material or volume, to become smaller
to incur a debt, obligation, or liability

nuance.ja: 名詞の contract は、単なる約束や了解ではなく、原則として法的拘束力を持つ合意を表す。ただし、成立要件、約因の必要性、書面・署名の要否などは法域と契約類型によって異なる。契約書という紙や電子文書を指すこともあるが、契約そのものと契約を証する文書は概念上同一とは限らない。動詞 contract は「契約する」のほか、contract a disease「病気にかかる」、muscles contract「筋肉が収縮する」の意味を持つ。名詞では第一音節、動詞では第二音節に強勢を置く。日本語の「委託する」に当たる意味で人を目的語にする場合、contract someone to do の形は使えるが、日常的には hire や commission の方が自然な場合もある。
nuance.en: As a noun, contract normally denotes an agreement intended and legally capable of creating enforceable rights or obligations rather than a merely social promise or informal understanding. Requirements concerning formation, consideration, writing, and signature vary by jurisdiction and type of transaction. Contract may also refer to the paper or electronic document recording the agreement, although the legal relationship and the document evidencing it are conceptually distinct. As a verb, contract also means acquire a disease or become physically smaller or tighter. The noun carries first-syllable stress, whereas the verb carries second-syllable stress. Contract someone to do something is possible for formally engaging a service provider, although hire or commission may be more natural in everyday contexts.

ja: contract：法的に強制可能な権利・義務を生じさせる契約、または契約する。
agreement：二者以上の合意を広く表し、必ずしも法的拘束力を持たない。
arrangement：当事者間で決めた実務上の取り決め。形式性・法的拘束力は文脈による。
covenant：一定の行為をする、またはしないという厳格・正式な約束や契約条項。
undertaking：特定の行為・義務を履行するという正式な約束。
hire：人を雇う、または報酬を払って物・サービスを一定期間利用する。
contract：動詞では、筋肉・物質などが収縮するという意味も持つ。
contract a disease：病気・感染症にかかる。病気と契約するという意味ではない。
en: a contract is a legally enforceable agreement, or contract means entering such an agreement.
an agreement broadly means a shared understanding and is not necessarily legally enforceable.
an arrangement is a practical understanding whose formality and legal force depend on context.
a covenant is a solemn or formal promise, often contained in a contract or deed.
an undertaking is a formal promise to perform or refrain from a particular act.
hire means employing someone or paying to use property or services for a period.
contract also means becoming physically shorter, tighter, or smaller.
contract a disease means becoming infected with or developing it, not making an agreement with it.

etymology.ja: contract はラテン語 contractus に由来し、これは contrahere「引き合わせる、集める、縮める、契約する」の過去分詞である。contrahere は con-「共に」と trahere「引く」から成る。「物を引き合わせる」という発想から、当事者を合意によって結び付ける「契約」の意味と、物理的に引き締める「収縮」の意味が発達した。病気にかかる意味は、病気や感染を自らの身に引き受けるという用法から生じた。
etymology.en: Contract derives from Latin contractus, the past participle of contrahere, meaning to draw together, collect, shorten, or make an agreement. Contrahere was formed from con-, together, and trahere, to draw. The idea of drawing things or people together developed into the legal sense of binding parties by agreement, while physical drawing together produced the sense of shrinking or tightening. The disease sense developed from the idea of acquiring or taking an illness upon oneself.

note.ja: 当事者間の合意を広く表すが、すべての agreement が法的に強制可能な contract になるとは限らない。
note.en: A broad term for mutual understanding; not every agreement constitutes a legally enforceable contract.

note.ja: 契約・証書に含まれる、行為または不作為についての正式で厳格な約束。
note.en: A formal and serious promise, often contained in a contract or deed, to act or refrain from acting.

note.ja: 義務の履行や一定の行為について与える正式な約束・確約。
note.en: A formal promise or assurance to perform an obligation or take a particular action.

note.ja: 物の大きさ・体積などが小さくなることを表す一般語で、物理的意味の contract に近い。
note.en: A general verb for becoming smaller in size or volume, corresponding to the physical sense of contract.

note.ja: 病気・性質・権利などを得ることを表し、acquire an infection は contract an infection より形式的に響く場合がある。
note.en: Means obtaining a disease, characteristic, or right; acquire an infection may sound more technical than contract an infection.

ja: The two companies entered into a five-year supply contract. — 両社は5年間の供給契約を締結した。
The contract requires the supplier to deliver the goods by the end of the month. — その契約は、供給業者に月末までの商品引渡しを義務付けている。
The museum contracted a specialist to restore the painting. — 美術館は、その絵画を修復するため専門家と契約した。
When exposed to cold temperatures, the material contracts slightly. — その材料は低温にさらされると、わずかに収縮する。
A patent license contract should clearly specify the licensed patents, permitted acts, territory, duration, and royalty obligations. — 特許ライセンス契約では、対象特許、許諾される行為、地域、期間およびロイヤルティー支払義務を明確に定めるべきである。
en: The two companies entered into a five-year supply contract.
The contract requires the supplier to deliver the goods by the end of the month.
The museum contracted a specialist to restore the painting.
When exposed to cold temperatures, the material contracts slightly.
A patent license contract should clearly specify the licensed patents, permitted acts, territory, duration, and royalty obligations.

grammar.countability: countable for a particular arrangement or document; uncountable for the state of agreeing or grammatical agreement
patterns: reach / conclude / enter into an agreement
be in agreement with + person / proposition

usage.consensus: Uncountable agreement means a shared opinion or the state of accepting the same position.
usage.arrangement: A countable agreement is a particular arrangement under which parties accept specified terms.
usage.document: Agreement may also refer to the written document recording the parties’ arrangement.
usage.legal_effect: Some agreements are legally enforceable contracts, while others are social, political, preliminary, or otherwise non-binding.
usage.prepositions: Use between for the participating parties, with for the other party, and on or about for the subject matter.
usage.infinitive: Agreement to do identifies an action that the parties have accepted: an agreement to supply goods.
usage.grammar_sense: In grammar, agreement means correspondence between related words in features such as number, person, or gender.
usage.drafting: Calling a document an agreement does not by itself conclusively determine its legal character or enforceability.

ja: 二人以上の人が同じ提案・条件・方針を受け入れること、合意
当事者間で取り決められた条件・約束
権利・義務などを定める協定・契約
合意内容を記載した書面
意見・判断・説明などが一致している状態
文法上、主語と動詞などの人称・数・性が一致すること
en: the act or state of two or more people accepting the same proposal, terms, or course of action
an arrangement containing terms or promises accepted by the parties
a contract or formal instrument establishing rights and obligations
a written document recording what the parties have agreed
the state of opinions, judgments, or accounts being consistent with one another
in grammar, correspondence between related words in person, number, gender, or another feature

nuance.ja: agreement は「同意している状態」から、具体的な取り決め、さらにその内容を記載した文書までを広く表す。contract は通常、法律上強制可能な権利・義務を生じさせる合意に焦点を置くが、agreement は友人同士の非公式な約束や政治的合意など、法的拘束力のないものも含み得る。したがって、Every contract is an agreement, but not every agreement is a contract. という整理が一般的に可能である。ただし、文書の表題が Agreement か Contract かだけで法的拘束力が決まるわけではない。in agreement は「同意して」、reach an agreement は「協議の結果、合意に達する」を意味する。文法では subject-verb agreement のように、語形の数・人称などの一致を表す。
nuance.en: Agreement broadly covers the state of agreeing, a particular arrangement, and the document recording that arrangement. Contract normally focuses on an agreement that creates legally enforceable rights or obligations, whereas agreement may also include an informal understanding between friends or a political arrangement without legal force. It is therefore generally possible to say that every contract is an agreement, but not every agreement is a contract. The title Agreement or Contract does not by itself determine whether a document is legally binding. In agreement means sharing the same view, while reach an agreement emphasizes successful completion of negotiation. In grammar, agreement describes correspondence in features such as number and person, as in subject-verb agreement.

ja: agreement：当事者間の合意・取り決めを広く表し、法的拘束力を持つとは限らない。
contract：原則として、法律上強制可能な権利・義務を生じさせる契約。
arrangement：実務上の方法・役割などについて決めた取り決め。
understanding：明示的な契約でなくても、当事者間に成立している了解。
accord：対立・交渉を経て成立した正式な合意。外交文脈でも使われる。
consensus：集団内で広く共有される意見・判断。
consent：特定の提案・行為を自由意思で承認すること。
settlement：紛争・訴訟・請求を終結させるための合意。
en: an agreement is a broad mutual understanding or arrangement and is not necessarily legally binding.
a contract normally creates rights or obligations enforceable by law.
an arrangement is a practical plan concerning how activities, responsibilities, or resources will be organized.
an understanding is an accepted position between parties that may not be expressly stated in a formal contract.
an accord is a formal agreement, often reached after disagreement or diplomatic negotiation.
consensus is an opinion or judgment broadly shared within a group.
consent is voluntary approval of a particular proposal, act, or request.
a settlement is an agreement that resolves a dispute, lawsuit, or claim.

etymology.ja: agreement は動詞 agree に、状態・結果・行為を表す接尾辞 -ment が付いて成立した。agree は古フランス語 agreer「喜ばせる、満足させる、同意する」に由来し、これは句 a gré「好みに、意にかなって」と関係する。gré はラテン語 gratus「喜ばしい、ありがたい」にさかのぼる。相手の提案が意にかなうという発想から、「同意する」「意見が一致する」という意味が発達した。
etymology.en: Agreement was formed from the verb agree with the noun-forming suffix -ment, which denotes a state, act, or result. Agree came from Old French agreer, meaning to please, satisfy, or consent, and is related to the phrase a gré, according to one’s pleasure. Gré ultimately derives from Latin gratus, pleasing or welcome. The idea that another person’s proposal was acceptable or pleasing developed into the meanings consent and hold the same opinion.

note.ja: 当事者が実務上の行動・役割・日程などについて決めた取り決め。
note.en: A practical understanding about conduct, responsibilities, schedules, or the organization of activities.

note.ja: 必ずしも正式な書面にされていない、当事者間の共通認識・了解。
note.en: A shared understanding between parties that is not necessarily expressed in a formal written document.

note.ja: 交渉・対立の後に成立した正式な合意を表し、国際関係でもよく用いられる。
note.en: A formal agreement, often reached after negotiation or conflict and commonly used in international relations.

note.ja: 集団の構成員の間で広く共有される意見・判断。
note.en: An opinion or judgment broadly shared among the members of a group.

note.ja: 法律上強制可能な権利・義務を生じさせる合意であり、agreement より法的意味が強い。
note.en: An agreement creating legally enforceable rights or obligations and therefore carrying a stronger legal implication.

ja: After several weeks of negotiation, the parties finally reached an agreement. — 数週間の交渉を経て、当事者たちはようやく合意に達した。
The agreement requires both companies to protect confidential information. — その契約は、両社に秘密情報の保護を義務付けている。
We are in agreement about the need to revise the schedule. — 日程を見直す必要があるという点で、私たちの意見は一致している。
Their informal agreement was never recorded in writing. — 彼らの非公式な取り決めは、一度も書面にされなかった。
A trademark coexistence agreement should define the permitted marks, goods, services, territories, and methods of use with sufficient precision. — 商標共存契約では、使用を認める商標、商品、役務、地域および使用方法を十分明確に定めるべきである。

The agreement requires both companies to protect confidential information.
We are in agreement about the need to revise the schedule.
Their informal agreement was never recorded in writing.
A trademark coexistence agreement should define the permitted marks, goods, services, territories, and methods of use with sufficient precision.
